question.problem:
Expressed in **ascending order** in radians, the exact solutions to the equation $4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-\frac{\pi }{6})+2=0,$ for $0<x<\pi ,$  are

${x}_{1}=$

question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-\frac{\pi }{6})+2 & =0 \\ 4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-\frac{\pi }{6}) & =-2 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-\frac{\pi }{6}) & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{2\pi }{3}+n\cdot 2\pi , & \, & \, & 3x-\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{4\pi }{3}+n\cdot 2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & =\frac{2\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{6}+n\cdot 2\pi  & \, & \, & 3x & =\frac{4\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{6}+n\cdot 2\pi  \\ 3x & =\frac{5\pi }{6}+n\cdot 2\pi  & \, & \, & 3x & =\frac{3\pi }{2}+n\cdot 2\pi  \\ x & =\frac{5\pi }{18}+n\cdot \frac{2\pi }{3} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\cdot \frac{2\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0<x<\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{5\pi }{18}$ and $x=\frac{\pi }{2}.$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{17\pi }{18}$ and $x=\frac{7\pi }{6}.$  We reject the solution $\frac{7\pi }{6}$ since it lies outside the domain of interest.

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0<x<\pi .$ 

So, in ascending order, the solutions are 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{5\pi }{18},\,{x}_{2}=\frac{\pi }{2},\,{x}_{3}=\frac{17\pi }{18}.
$$
